name: Meadow-Tempest
description: Meadow-Tempest orbits a binary star system, and the interplay of two stellar gravitational fields gives its atmosphere a turbulence that defies modeling. Its bands are unusually wide and soft-edged, blending into each other in gradients of pale green and yellow that resemble a sunlit meadow viewed from above, an impression shattered by the violence of the storms that churn within those deceptively peaceful colors. The binary sunset paints the upper atmosphere in double shadows that create visual effects found nowhere else in charted space.

The dual stellar heating creates temperature differentials within the atmosphere that drive wind speeds in excess of any recorded on a single-star gas giant. The storms on Meadow-Tempest are not merely large, they are fast, with jet streams that circle the planet in hours and cyclonic systems that form and dissipate with startling rapidity. The orbital debris ring, composed of captured asteroids and the remains of three moons torn apart by tidal forces, adds a glittering halo to a world already spectacular in its violence.

No biological activity has been detected on Meadow-Tempest, though the atmospheric chemistry includes complex organic molecules that suggest prebiotic conditions. The binary star system's gravitational complexity has kept the planet's orbit stable through a mechanism that astrophysicists have not fully explained, and the system serves as a laboratory for orbital mechanics research. Early colonial surveys classified it as a fuel depot candidate, but the atmospheric turbulence has deterred all harvesting attempts.

Meadow-Tempest's helium-3 reserves are estimated to be among the largest in the sector, making the harvesting problem a matter of considerable commercial interest. Several engineering firms have proposed deep-atmosphere collection platforms designed to ride the jet streams rather than fight them, but none have progressed beyond the simulation stage. The dual-star gravitational effects create periodic windows of relative atmospheric calm, and timing a harvest operation to these windows may eventually prove feasible if the models can be trusted.
